text.p: Following are the main stories in today's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALL newspapers lead with with Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad saying local funds should come in to buy shares which has fallen to "bargain" levels.
-- PM Mahathir said he was made to understand that the delay in construction of the new Kuala Lumpur airport was not critical and it would be ready before the Commonwealth Games in late 1998.
-- Bank Negara Governor Ahmad Don has not resigned from his post, a central bank spokesman said, denying market rumours.

-- National carmaker Proton expects another profitable year but says rate of earnings growth may not be as spectacular as recorded in previous financial year. Proton reported pretax earnings jump of 126.4 percent to 1.03 billion ringgit for the year to March 31, 1997.
-- The government is studying a report on the Bakun dam contract said to be the cause of dispute between project developer Ekran and its main contractor.
